tradeoff: jellyscale's tests named Octave (formerly Fluster): the CORS tests used its WebView origins, two docs checks pinned an Octave row in docs/status.md, and the search-hints audit required its evidence to name Octave's issue. Given up: nothing a viewer has; the CORS checks cover a custom-scheme origin and localhost origins as before.
entry: No jellyscale test names, runs or records Octave (owner, 2026-11-20: 'We shouldn't include Octave in our testing'). The CORS tests use generic origins (app://localhost, http://app.localhost, https://app.localhost); the checks that pinned an Octave row in docs/status.md (compat TestOctaveHasOneRowThatSaysItHasNotBeenRun, internal/api TestStatusHasAnOctaveRowThatNamesTheRecordAndDoesNotCallItWorking) are removed; the search-hints audit no longer requires its evidence to name Octave's issue. The docs may still describe Octave as jellyscale's own client (D-031). Recorded Jellyfin captures keep the origins they were made with, since they record what Jellyfin did. Extends D-027.
